newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa revenue service offers tax relief plan.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa revenue service offers tax relief plan.

text.p: The South African Revenue Service said on Wednesday it would grant relief to certain categories of people to encourage defaulting taxpayers to put their tax affairs in order before the end of February.

Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus said in a statement the tax relief programme allowed defaulters a "window of opportunity" to bring their tax affairs up to date without incurring severe penalties that the government could impose.
To maximise resources and encourage the greatest number of applications to come forward, the SARS will not tax qualifying applicants prior to March 1, 1994.
"Our objective is to legitimise the tax affairs of as many people as possible and to make the process attractive to defaulters," said Piet Liebenberg, SARS chief executive officer.
He said he was confident most people would appreciate the significant leeway being afforded to them, particularily people whose liability went back many years.

"Without the benfits offered them through this relief programme, they would be far worse off. So, we trust many will weigh up these benefits and grasp the opportunity to get their affairs in order at the lowest possible cost to themselves," Liebenberg said.
South Africa this year amalgamated inland revenue and customs and excise under the new SARS in an effort to improve efficiency and draw more taxpayers into the tax net.
